title: GPGPU Water Surface Wave Simulation
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a GPU-accelerated water surface wave simulation. Use DataTexture to store the height field and update the wave equation every frame through a custom shader.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Water Surface Height-Field Model]

Use two 256×256 DataTextures (FloatType, RGBAFormat) to store the height fields for the current frame and the previous frame:
- currentHeightMap: current-frame height h(t)
- previousHeightMap: previous-frame height h(t-dt)

Wave equation (finite-difference discretization):
  h(x,y,t+dt) = 2·h(x,y,t) - h(x,y,t-dt) + c²·dt²·∇²h(x,y,t)
  where ∇²h = (h(x+1,y) + h(x-1,y) + h(x,y+1) + h(x,y-1) - 4·h(x,y)) / dx²
  dx = 1/256

Damping: multiply the new height by the damping coefficient every frame
  h_new *= damping

Parameters:
- Wave speed c = 2.0
- Damping damping = 0.995 (adjustable)
- Viscosity factor viscosity = 0.3 (apply additional high-frequency attenuation during the Laplacian calculation: h_new = h_new * (1 - viscosity) + avg_neighbors * viscosity)
- Time step dt = 1/60

Per-frame update logic (use WebGLRenderTarget to implement ping-pong double buffering):
1. Use a full-screen quad plus a custom fragment shader to read currentHeightMap and previousHeightMap
2. Compute the new height value in the shader and output it to a RenderTarget
3. Swap current and previous
4. Also compute a normal map from the height field in the shader using central differences

Alternatively, calculate the DataTexture directly on the CPU (if the GPU approach is too complex), but the resolution must remain 256×256 and the real-time frame rate must be > 15fps.

[Interaction: Click to Generate Ripples]
Click the water surface with the mouse (use a Raycaster to detect the plane intersection) → add a circular disturbance around the hit position within a radius=5 grid-cell range:
  For a cell at a distance of d grid cells from the hit point: h += amplitude * cos(π·d/(2·radius))²  (where d < radius)
  amplitude = 0.3

[Wind Effect]
When windToggle is enabled: apply a small offset in the +x direction every frame
  h(x+1,y,t) += 0.001·h(x,y,t) (approximation)
  This causes waves to propagate faster in the +x direction

[Rendering]
(1) Water surface mesh: 256×256 PlaneGeometry; update each vertex's y coordinate from the height field every frame (or use displacementMap)
(2) Water surface material: MeshPhysicalMaterial or MeshStandardMaterial
    - metalness: 0.1, roughness: 0.05
    - Use a normalMap derived from the height field
    - Color: #1565C0 (deep blue)
    - Environment map: use PMREMGenerator to generate a simple environment map from a gradient (sky blue→white)
    - Translucent: opacity=0.85, transparent=true
(3) Lighting: DirectionalLight(white, 1.0) shining from (5,10,5) + AmbientLight(0.3)
(4) Ground (beneath the water surface): a simple dark-colored plane
(5) OrbitControls

[HUD and Controls]
(6) HUD in the upper-left corner:
  - Maximum wave height (id="maxHeight")
  - Wave energy (id="waveEnergy"): defined as Σ h(x,y)² summed over all grid cells
  - Frame number (id="frameNum")

(7) Damping slider (id="dampingSlider"): range from 0.98 to 1.0, step 0.001, default 0.995
(8) Wind toggle (id="windToggle"): checkbox, disabled by default

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
  - maxHeight: maximum absolute value in the current frame's height field
  - waveEnergy: Σ h² over all grid cells
  - frameNum: frame counter (incrementing from 0)
  - dampingValue: current damping value
  - windEnabled: whether wind is enabled (boolean)
  - gridSize: grid size (256)

Output a single HTML file.
